subject: Surge buffer pricing and temporary overrun plan
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@fastretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected weekend surge + short term capacity request

Hi Hannah —

We had a much larger-than-forecasted traffic spike over the weekend tied to our promotion. We burned through our daily quota and several customer-facing jobs were throttled. Our engineering team smoothed the load but we need a short-term fix while we finalize an architecture change.

Can Redwood provide: 
- a temporary quota uplift (for ~72 hours) and a clear overrun rate we can accept immediately
- or an alternative option that avoids immediate overage invoices landing on our PO queue

I've attached our rough hourly forecast for the last week. We can sign a short amendment if you can provide a capped surcharge or a bundled "surge protection" arrangement for the month.

We need something that procurement can sign quickly (PO or SOW amendment). Budget owner is in this thread.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering
FastRetail

Attachment: fastretail_monthly_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected weekend surge + short term capacity request

Hi Alice —

Sorry you hit that spike — glad your team mitigated it. We have two pragmatic paths that have worked well for other customers: 

1) Short window headroom (fast lift): we provision a temporary quota uplift for a defined window (e.g., 72h). Billing options: pay-as-you-go overrun rate (per-token) or a flat uplift fee. We can cap the total uplift spend so procurement gets a predictable PO line.

2) Surge Shield pilot (recommended for recurring event patterns): a monthly "spike-shield" add-on that provides a buffer (X TCUs) with a reduced surcharge rate and a small flat fee. This is amortized across the month and avoids surprise single-day invoices. It requires a one-page amendment.

For FastRetail specifically, given your forecast and velocity, I suggest a 72h uplift plus a concurrent Surge Shield pilot for the remainder of October. Proposed commercial terms are in the attached matrix — it includes a discounted surcharge at 60% of our standard overrun rate when you opt into the pilot.

Next steps: 
- If procurement prefers a capped uplift PO, we can send a short SOW amendment and invoice the uplift as a single flat charge.
- If you want the Surge Shield pilot, we'll need a signed one-page amendment (DocuSign link) and a PO for the pilot fee.

I've looped Ben (finance) to confirm acceptable discount bands. I can get legal involved if procurement needs specific contract language.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_pricing_matrix.xlsx (pricing matrix, 18KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: margin check on FastRetail surge concession

Hannah —

Reviewed the proposed matrix. We can do a temporary uplift + 40% discount off list overrun rate for the pilot if: 
- pilot term is max 30 days
- total uplift spend is capped in the amendment (no open-ended invoices)
- procurement agrees to a PO for the pilot fee up front

If procurement pushes for a deeper discount, we should convert to a short-term committed uplift (30-day min) with blended unit pricing.

Neha, are there any billing/ops constraints for doing a capped uplift with invoice smoothing?

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
